Container operations

On a Docker installation of SATOM, restart a service of the stack, switch the node to another release and install the proxy certificate — all through the optional operations agent.

👤 ForAdministratorAdvanced user
🔑 Permissionsusers.manage
📍 WhereGlobal ADOM → Administrator → Container operations, shown only on a container node (URL /system/container/)

What is it?#

Container operations is the administration page for a SATOM node that runs as a Docker stack. It is the container counterpart of Software Update, the Services card in Settings and the node certificate in Node TLS. The page itself never touches Docker: every button only queues a request, and a separate, optional container — the operations agent — re-checks the request against a closed list and does the work.

What does it do?#

  • Shows the state of the Operations agent (live, not answering, not enabled), its version and the stack's version.
  • Lists which host-only Capabilities the agent currently performs for this node.
  • Services of this stack — start, stop or restart the allowed services.
  • Update — switch this node to another SATOM release (X.Y.Z), with automatic rollback if the console does not come back healthy.
  • Proxy certificate — install a certificate and private key into the TLS proxy and reload it.
  • Recent agent requests — the last 15 requests with their steps and result.

On a host (non-container) installation the page only says: "This node is a host install. Its services, updates and certificate are managed from Settings → Services, Software Update and Node certificate."

Requirements#

  • SATOM runs in the container runtime. The menu entry only appears there.
  • For any action, the operations agent must be enabled and live (it reported a heartbeat within the last 60 seconds). Without it the page opens, explains why, and offers nothing.
  • Update additionally needs the installer layout (a node set up with the installer, not a manual checkout).

⚠️Warning — The agent is root on the host

The agent mounts the Docker socket: whoever controls it is root on the host. It is therefore optional and off unless you enable it (run the installer again and answer yes to the operations agent, or set SATOM_SETUP_AGENT=yes for a manual checkout).

Permissions#

Every route of this page — the page, its status polling, and each action — requires users.manage (Administrator). Without it the page answers 403, and the menu entry is not shown (the whole Administrator group is drawn only for users.manage).

Where it is reachable. The menu entry is in the Global ADOM's Administrator group. The page also opens in the FortiWeb ADOM by URL; in the FortiADC, FortiAnalyzer and FortiAuthenticator ADOMs it redirects to that ADOM's home page.

How to use#

Read the agent card#

Badge Meaning
live The agent reported within the last 60 s. The card shows Last heartbeat, Agent version, stack version and Layout (installer or manual).
not answering The agent is enabled but silent (or has never reported). The card shows the reason and "Nothing is queued while the agent is silent. On the host:" satom-docker ps agent · satom-docker logs agent.
not enabled The stack runs without the agent. The card explains how to enable it.

Under live you may see agent and stack differ — an update recreates every service except the agent, so run satom-docker up -d on the host to bring it to the stack version — and, on a manual layout, updates from the console need the installer layout.

The Capabilities card lists self_update, service_control, cert_activation, unit_health and ha_promote, each via agent or unavailable with the reason. The first four are via agent exactly while the agent is live; ha_promote is always unavailable in the container runtime.

Restart, stop or start a service#

  1. In Services of this stack, find the service.
  2. Press one of the buttons in Actions (restart, stop or start, depending on the service and its state).
  3. Confirm the browser prompt (<action> <service>?).
  4. The page follows the request and reloads when it finishes, with the request highlighted in Recent agent requests.
Service Label Actions allowed
web Web application restart only
scheduler Scheduler start, stop, restart
cron Periodic jobs start, stop, restart
proxy TLS proxy (nginx) restart only
postgres PostgreSQL restart only
redis Redis (rate limits) restart only
victoria-metrics Metrics store restart only

A running service offers restart and stop (where allowed); a stopped one offers start, or restart where restart is its only action. The agent itself and the one-shot tls-init job are never controllable. A service with no container shows no container and no buttons.

ℹ️Note

Restarting web or proxy interrupts the page for a moment. The page keeps polling through the gap.

Update this node#

  1. In Update, check the running version (The stack runs …) and the releases Already on this host (tree only = the source is present but not the image).
  2. Type the version, e.g. 2.3.1.
  3. Type UPDATE in the confirmation box.
  4. Press Update this node.
  5. Wait: the console restarts during the update; the page keeps polling and reloads when the request finishes.

On a primary + standby pair, update the primary first (schema changes can only be applied on the writable primary), then the standby. Releases without the operations agent are refused here; switch to them with satom-setup.sh on the host.

Install the proxy certificate#

  1. In Proxy certificate, choose Certificate (PEM), Private key (PEM) and optionally Chain (optional).
  2. Press Install and reload the proxy.
  3. The result appears next to the button: installed: · days, or the reason for the refusal.

Configuration#

Field Description Required Example
Version Target release, X.Y.Z (a leading v is ignored) Yes (update) 2.3.1
type UPDATE Typed confirmation; must be exactly UPDATE Yes (update) UPDATE
Certificate (PEM) Server certificate file Yes (certificate) server.crt
Private key (PEM) Matching private key Yes (certificate) server.key
Chain (optional) Intermediate chain No chain.pem

The update and certificate controls are disabled when the agent is not live; the update controls are also disabled on a manual layout.

Example#

🧪Example — Recover the scheduler on a Docker node

Scheduled actions stopped firing. On Container operations the agent is live and the Scheduler row shows a red badge. Press restart, confirm restart scheduler?, and wait. The page reloads with a ctr-restart request for scheduler · restart in Recent agent requests, state success, and the Scheduler badge is green again.

Result#

  • Each action writes a status row (state queued) and a request file that the agent picks up. Recent agent requests shows Request id, Kind (ctr-restart, ctr-update, ctr-cert), Target, By, State (success, failed, or in yellow queued/running) and a Log of every step with ✓ or ✗.
  • After a start or restart the agent waits up to 3 minutes for the service to be running and healthy.
  • An update downloads the release if it is not on the host, loads the image the release publishes (checked against its checksum and its version; built on the host only when the release publishes none), recreates every service except the agent, reloads the proxy, and waits up to 7 minutes for the web service to become healthy. If it does not, the stack is switched back to the previous release and image. The update takes no backup and the rollback does not restore the database — back up first (see System backup).
  • A certificate install waits up to 90 seconds for the agent's verdict. The private key travels only inside the request, never in the status row the page lists.
  • The Audit log records container_ops.service, container_ops.update and container_ops.cert.

Troubleshooting#

"type UPDATE to confirm"#

Possible causes - The confirmation box does not contain exactly UPDATE.

Solution 1. Type UPDATE (upper case) and press Update this node again.

Verification - A new ctr-update row appears in Recent agent requests.

"version must be X.Y.Z"#

Possible causes - The version is empty or not three numbers separated by dots.

Solution 1. Enter a version such as 2.3.1.

Verification - The request is queued instead of refused.

"The operations agent is enabled but not answering (…)"#

Possible causes - The agent container is stopped or its heartbeat is older than 60 seconds, or its time stamp is in the future (clock problem).

Solution 1. On the host, run satom-docker ps agent and satom-docker logs agent. 2. Recreate it with satom-docker up -d.

Verification - The agent badge shows live and the capabilities show via agent.

"… is not allowed on '…' from this console"#

Possible causes - The action is not in the service's allowed list (for example a stop on web, proxy or postgres), or the service is the agent or tls-init.

Solution 1. Use an allowed action from the table above, or act on the host with satom-docker.

Verification - The button offered on the page is accepted.

"cert and key PEM files are required"#

Possible causes - The certificate or the key file was not selected.

Solution 1. Select both Certificate (PEM) and Private key (PEM) and try again.

Verification - The result reads installed: ….

A request ended "failed" with "request expired: queued … s ago (limit 600 s)"#

Possible causes - The agent picked the request up more than 10 minutes after it was queued. It does not run a restart or an update late.

Solution 1. Check that the agent is live, then send the request again.

Verification - The new request reaches success.

An update ended "failed" with "the update did not come up healthy; rolled back"#

Possible causes - The web service did not become healthy within 7 minutes on the new release.

Solution 1. Read the steps in the Log column of the request. 2. Fix the cause on the host before trying again.

Verification - The stack version in the agent card is the release you expect.

Advanced#

Advanced How requests travel

The web container has no Docker socket. A request is a JSON file in the node's update-request queue plus a status file; both directories are volumes shared with the agent. The allowlist of services and actions exists twice — in the web application, so the page only offers what the agent accepts, and in the agent itself, which is the security boundary and re-validates every request. Nothing is queued while the agent is silent, so nothing fires later by surprise.

Advanced Runtime detection

The container runtime is selected only when the environment variable SATOM_RUNTIME is exactly container; anything else means a host install. The agent counts as declared when SATOM_AGENT=docker. After an action the page polls /system/container/status/<id> every 3 seconds until the request is final; a JSON summary of the agent and service state is also available at /system/container/state.

Advanced Service failures

After a start or restart, a service that is not running and healthy within 3 minutes fails the request with " did not come back: …". A service with no container in the stack is refused with "service '' has no container in this stack".
